reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Art as the Path to Individuation", "body": "Mario traces Symbolic Studies back to childhood doodling, a Kubrick obsession that carried him into film school, and a later turn toward tarot, and he argues that art is the key to individuation, that being an artist is doing your shadow work, and that creativity and freedom are inseparable. He cites Crowley's line that destruction is the first act of creation, and says his own finished pieces keep teaching him things he never intended months after he made them. Chance, a former film studies minor, adds that it almost doesn't matter what you create, only that you do."}, {"title": "Simulacra and the Map That Replaced the Land", "body": "Mario read Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulation for a small book club and now uses the word model for it: the models handed to us about how the sky, science and reality work eventually flip into their opposites, so news outlets mislead and schools blunt knowledge. He points to cartography, where copies of copies made the map realer than the land it described, and notes how often modern maps crop the poles away. Chance frames the same idea through screens, saying we accept truth from black mirror scrying devices and let that overlay filter out what our own senses report."}, {"title": "Polar Gods Made Solar", "body": "Mario's central claim is that deities we now file as solar were revered as polar first, with Mercury the clearest case: the Magician lifting his wand, the phallus, the caduceus rod with its two snakes, and by extension Hermes and Thoth. He reads the spine and its 33 vertebrae as the same pole expressed in the body, and the toroid's center as the trunk of the world tree and a gateway between realms. Chance layers initiation on top of it, describing a literal story, then a solar one, then a polar one, then the truth that all of it exists within you."}, {"title": "Earth Shape Agnosticism and the Apophatic Method", "body": "Mario dates his interest to 2014, reading Eric Dubay on a flight to India, and the story he tells is of a young man in Mumbai who volunteered, unprompted, that his guru teaches a stationary Earth. He calls himself agnostic about the shape and more interested in whether the realm is geocentric. Chance answers with method rather than a model, arguing that truth is approached apophatically by ruling out what it is not, that one inversion at the base of a worldview leaves everything above it unstable, and that a source caught lying a dozen times has earned no further trust."}, {"title": "The External Savior and Taking Responsibility", "body": "Chance builds the closing argument: if the solar perspective is at root a feminine, goddess oriented one, it explains the sacrificial streak in ancient sun cults and, he suggests, reappears in the external savior at the heart of communism and of the redeemer myth, where a solar deity dies for everyone and sets the example. His counter is that if everyone sacrifices themselves nobody is left, so the heroic move is to take responsibility for your own freedom. Mario had already supplied the psychology, noting that when everything is external you stop trusting your own senses."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies argues that every major deity in antiquity was originally a polar god before the solar model was imposed over them, and Baudrillard's simulacra explains exactly how that inversion was achieved and kept in place.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Covers polar cosmology as the original paradigm buried by the heliocentric model, Mercury and Hermes and Thoth as inherently polar gods with the caduceus as the axis mundi, the spine's 33 vertebrae as the body's polar column, Baudrillard's simulacra and how the solar perspective instills external psychological dependency, the Norse inversion of sun and moon polarity, art as the path of individuation, and the Thoth Tarot Art card as destruction and transformation at the root of creative freedom.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Great Bear as the Original Sky Clock", "body": "Mario lays out his case that the circumpolar Dippers, wheeling around Polaris and visible all year from much of the world, once served as a seven-stationed sky clock older than both the solar ecliptic and lunar reckoning. He notes that roughly 90 percent of the world's population can see the Pole Star, traces veiled references in Lovecraftian black magic groups that time their workings for when the Great Bear hangs from its tail, and links the Egyptian opening of the mouth ritual and its seven-shaped adze tool to Ursa Major, while Chance adds that the bear gives us our bearing."}, {"title": "Seven Turns, Black Cubes, and the Merkabah", "body": "Mario catalogs ascension rituals built on the number seven and on turning: merkavah mystics riding the chariot north to a Solomon's Temple in the sky, pilgrims circling the black cube of the Kaaba seven times, the Jewish tefillin strap wound seven times up the arm, and the Chinese Pace of Yu that walks the stars of Ursa Major, each star standing for a planet. Chance counters that circling a cube may externalize one's authority, while the Merkabah, pictured as six points around one, describes a centered being, like the charioteer who sits inside the cube instead of going around it."}, {"title": "Occultism as Training for a Good Death", "body": "Mario shares a growing hunch that much of occultism is a veiled death practice, and that groups like the Freemasons, through their tracing boards, may be preserving instructions for how to die properly and ascend, a reading he now wonders about for the Major Arcana too. Chance connects this to the heathen ideal of an honorable death, suggests that dying right may mean having the rite right, and asks whether a soul whose vessel floats rather than sinks in the waters of forgetfulness can return remembering, while solar cults that deny reincarnation may be producing a forgetful, servile class."}, {"title": "The Isis Thesis and the Horns of the Bull", "body": "Mario credits the YouTuber behind Occult Lectures for pointing him to The Isis Thesis by Judy K. King, which decodes the Egyptian afterlife as a journey east that circles toward the north, aiming for the cusp of the magnetosphere, the hyperbola of the toroid that the Egyptians pictured as the horns of the bull, with a spiritual double met only at a set stage. Chance reads the author's name for hidden meaning and likens each fertilized egg to a being ascending one rung of the fractal ladder, and Mario agrees the name may be a pen name for a group."}, {"title": "Kumbh, Kneph, and Aquarius as the Holy Vessel", "body": "Mario tells how two opposing parties of demigods churned the ocean of milk with the serpent Vasuki wrapped around a central mountain, producing a nectar held in a pot called the kumbh, whose spilled drops gave rise to the Kumbh Mela, a river festival that drew 120 million people over two months and which he calls deeply Aquarian. Chance ties the kumbh to the Egyptian Kneph, or Khnum, the potter who shapes Osiris on his wheel, and Mario adds that Aquarius in India is called Khnum and that some sources name Aquarius the light bearer rather than the water bearer."}]
